## Problems with the memory test (or rather, with exclusions based on the 
#   memory test)

(1) Learning experiment
    - People who have memory rates < 50 % have in fact learned something
    - Stimuli have (possibly) contradicting features
    - If at all, memory rates of ~ 50 % would be problematic

(2) Information integration:
    - People are told to form an attitude regarding brands (logos)
    - Best participants are probably those that integrate information
    - If integration is successful, there is no memory for the qualifiers

    => We would probably lose more people in the apply condition as one would
       expect information integration to be more likely there
    => Compensation of these selective dropouts by naturally lower importance of
       and therefore worse memory for qualifiers in ignore condition

(3) Interindividual differences in "true" p_c, p_u, and a parameters / reliance
    on the different strategies
    - Forgetting the qualifiers is probably most likely when evaluations are not
      formed via propositions, but associative
    - Selective dropouts of people that rely more on associative process
       
    => Artefactual decrease of a estimate
    => Potential in- or deflation of p_c and p_u
    => Worse model fit

# However: Bading et al. (2025): 
  "better memory for assimilative than for contrastive propositions 
   produces inflated C parameter estimates (in comparison to the actual 
   size of the co-occurrence effect)..."
    - This statement is made only for "apply" condition. Here, for us, the
      propositional processes cannot be distinguished, i.e. (roughly) an
      inflation of c corresponds to an inflation of a for us?!

  "strongly inflated C parameters when overall memory levels are high, 
   but produce only weakly inflated C parameter estimates when overall 
   memory levels are low"
    - We have low memory rates (speaking in terms of random guessing, at least)


## Empirical argument
  valence accuracy ~ memory
    -> memory should not predict correct attitude formation
